en: to slant; to move slantwise; to tilt

examples.en: The child tilted his head and looked at me.

examples.ko: 이해가 안 되는지 친구가 머리를 갸우뚱했어요.
examples.en: My friend tilted her head as if she didn't understand.
The puppy hears a sound and tilts its head.

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고도 다들 고개를 갸우뚱거렸어요.
examples.en: Even after hearing that, everyone kept tilting their heads in doubt.

examples.ko: 선생님은 제 답을 보고 고개를 갸우뚱하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher looked at my answer and tilted his head.

examples.ko: 갸우뚱하게 서 있던 의자가 결국 넘어졌어요.
examples.en: The chair that was standing at a tilt finally fell over.

explain: 거의 '고개를 갸우뚱하다'로 쓰고, 이해가 안 되거나 궁금하거나 의심스러울 때 나오는 동작이에요. '갸웃하다', '갸웃거리다'도 비슷해요. '-거리다'를 붙이면 여러 번 반복하는 느낌이 나요.

phrases.en: The child looked at the picture, tilting his head again and again.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-거리다'가 붙어 고개를 여러 번 기울이는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -거리다 it feels like tilting the head repeatedly.

phrases.example: 그 말을 듣고 친구가 고개를 갸웃했어요.
phrases.en: Hearing that, my friend tilted his head slightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '갸우뚱하다'보다 조금 가볍게 한 번 기울이는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A slightly lighter, single tilt compared with 갸우뚱하다.

phrases.en: The puppy looks at me with its head tilted.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 이어서 다른 동작과 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -며 it joins the tilting to another action.

explain_en: It is almost always used as '고개를 갸우뚱하다', the gesture you make when you don't understand, are curious or doubtful. '갸웃하다' and '갸웃거리다' are similar. Adding '-거리다' gives a sense of repeating the motion.

examples.en: I knelt down in front of my parents to apologize.

examples.ko: 바닥에 꿇어앉아서 이십 분 동안 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I knelt on the floor and waited for twenty minutes.

examples.ko: 한복을 입고 방석 위에 꿇어앉아 인사했어요.
examples.en: Wearing a hanbok, I knelt on a cushion and bowed.

examples.ko: 무릎이 아파서 오래 꿇어앉아 있기 힘들어요.
examples.en: My knees hurt, so it's hard to stay kneeling for long.
The child knelt down and looked the puppy in the eye.

examples.ko: 어른 앞에서도 꼭 꿇어앉지 않아도 돼요.
examples.en: You don't have to kneel even in front of elders.

explain: 무릎을 바닥에 대고 앉는 자세예요. 사과, 벌, 예절 같은 정해진 상황에서 주로 써서 일상 대화에서는 자주 나오지 않아요. 비슷한 '무릎을 꿇다'는 '굴복하다'라는 뜻으로도 써요.

phrases.en: As punishment, they kneel at the front of the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꿇어앉다'의 해요체로 지금이나 습관적인 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form, used for current or habitual actions.

phrases.en: The child knelt and apologized.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꿇어앉다'와 비슷하고, '굴복하다'라는 뜻으로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '꿇어앉다', and it can also mean to give in.
phrases.en_equiv: to get down on one's knees

phrases.en: I stayed kneeling for a long time, so my legs are numb.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아 있다'를 붙여 그 자세를 계속 유지한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아 있다' shows you stay in that posture.

explain_en: It describes sitting with your knees on the floor. It is used mostly in set situations such as apologizing, punishment, or showing etiquette, so it is not very common in daily talk. The similar '무릎을 꿇다' can also mean to give in or surrender.

examples.en: Grandma's way of speaking is always warm and slow.
Slow music was playing, so I felt sleepy.

examples.ko: 그 가게 주인은 행동이 조금 느릿해요.
examples.en: The shop owner moves a little slowly.
The river is flowing slowly.

examples.ko: 더워서 그런지 오늘은 모든 게 느릿해 보여요.
examples.en: Maybe because of the heat, everything looks slow today.

examples.ko: 느릿한 걸음으로 공원을 한 바퀴 돌았어요.
examples.en: I walked around the park once at a leisurely pace.

explain: '느리다'보다 여유 있고 느긋한 느낌이 있어서 걸음, 말씨, 음악의 속도를 부드럽게 표현할 때 써요. '느릿느릿하다'보다 덜 답답한 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '느리다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: His slow way of speaking is his charm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말의 속도가 느긋하고 부드러운 느낌일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when speech is slow in a soft and relaxed way.

phrases.en: I walked slowly in the park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서두르지 않고 천천히 움직일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving slowly without hurrying.

phrases.en: Listening to a slow song makes me feel at ease.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡의 속도가 느린 것을 부드럽게 표현해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft way to say a song's tempo is slow.

explain_en: It feels more leisurely than '느리다', so it softly describes the pace of steps, speech or music. It sounds less frustrating than '느릿느릿하다'. In everyday talk, '느리다' is used more.

examples.en: The child smiles broadly after getting a present.
My younger sibling is beaming after seeing the test score.
My father has been smiling happily since morning.
The baby saw its mother and smiled broadly.

examples.ko: 뭐가 그렇게 좋아서 혼자 벙글벙글 웃어요?
examples.en: What makes you so happy that you are grinning to yourself?
The whole family was beaming at the news of the acceptance.

explain: 소리 없이 기분 좋게 환하게 웃는 모습에 써요. '벙글벙글 웃다/하다' 형태로 자주 나와요. '싱글벙글'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The child runs over with a big smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: '벙글벙글'과 거의 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 더 흔히 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 벙글벙글 and more common in daily speech.

phrases.example: 좋은 소식을 듣고 하루 종일 벙글벙글해요.
phrases.en: I've been beaming all day after hearing good news.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웃다' 없이 '-하다'만 붙여서 기분 좋은 상태를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -하다 alone, without 웃다, shows a happy state.

phrases.en: The baby smiles brightly when it sees me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의성어·의태어가 아닌 일반적인 말이라 어떤 상황에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A general expression, not a mimetic word, so it fits any situation.

explain_en: It describes smiling brightly and happily without much sound, often as '벙글벙글 웃다/하다'. '싱글벙글' is used in much the same way and is very common in daily speech.

examples.en: Grandfather smiled gently when he saw his grandchild.

examples.ko: 그녀는 대답 대신 빙그레 미소만 지었어요.
examples.en: She answered with only a quiet smile instead of words.
The child smiled softly after being praised.
Everyone smiled warmly at the good news.
The teacher nodded with a gentle smile.
Dad smiled softly while reading the letter.

explain: '빙그레'는 입을 벌리지 않고 소리 없이 부드럽게 웃는 모양이에요. 소리 내어 크게 웃는 '하하'나 '깔깔'과 달라요. '빙그레 웃다', '빙그레 미소를 짓다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Mom nodded with a gentle smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃으면서 다른 행동을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to link another action with a smile.

phrases.en: The baby's gently smiling face is cute.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웃는'으로 활용하면 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the form 웃는, it can describe the noun that follows.

phrases.en: The teacher praised us with a gentle smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: '웃다'보다 조금 더 부드럽고 글 같은 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Slightly softer and more literary than 웃다.

explain_en: 빙그레 describes a soft smile made without opening the mouth and without sound. It is different from loud laughter like 하하 or 깔깔. It appears in phrases like 빙그레 웃다 and 빙그레 미소를 짓다.

examples.en: I heard the whisper of the wind in the forest.
My heart pounded at his whisper.

examples.ko: 아이들의 속삭임 때문에 수업이 조금 시끄러웠어요.
examples.en: The children's whispering made the class a little noisy.

examples.ko: 도서관에서는 속삭임처럼 작은 소리로 말해야 해요.
examples.en: In the library you must speak as quietly as a whisper.
The sound of whispering grew louder.
I was startled when I heard my friend's whisper.

explain: 속삭임은 작게 소곤소곤 말하는 소리와 그 분위기에 써요. '귓속말'은 남이 못 듣게 귀에 대고 하는 말이고, 속삭임은 소리 자체를 말해요. '바람의 속삭임'처럼 시나 노래에도 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 친구가 제 귀에 대고 작게 속삭였어요.
phrases.en: My friend whispered softly into my ear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '속삭임'의 동사형으로, 작게 소곤소곤 말하는 행동을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the verb form of 속삭임 and describes the act of whispering.

phrases.en: His sweet whispers weakened my resolve.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사랑이나 유혹의 분위기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a common pairing in romantic or tempting situations.

phrases.en: I whispered in my friend's ear during class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 귓속말은 남이 못 듣게 귀에 대고 하는 말이라 소리보다 행동에 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: 귓속말 is words said into someone's ear so others can't hear, so it is more about the act than the sound.

explain_en: 속삭임 is the sound and mood of speaking softly in a low voice. A '귓속말' is words said into someone's ear so others can't hear, while 속삭임 is about the sound itself. It also appears often in poems and songs, like '바람의 속삭임'.

en: this way and that; from every angle

examples.en: The child plays, turning the toy this way and that.
The cat dodged my hand this way and that.
I looked over the clothes from every angle in front of the mirror.
The road was jammed, so I wove through the alleys.

examples.ko: 문제를 요리조리 생각해 봐도 답을 모르겠어요.
examples.en: I've thought about the problem every which way, but I don't know the answer.
The fish slipped out of the net, darting this way and that.

explain: '아무렇게나'가 아니라 이쪽저쪽 방향을 바꾸며 움직이거나 살필 때 써요. 조금 귀엽고 가벼운 말투예요. 아이나 동물의 움직임에 특히 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: He looked at the watch from every angle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 방향에서 자세히 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looking closely from many directions.

phrases.en: The child dodges this way and that while running away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직이면서 이쪽저쪽으로 피하는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes dodging by moving from side to side.
phrases.en_equiv: to dodge this way and that

phrases.en: The puppy runs around here and there.
phrases.nuance_ko: '요리조리'와 비슷하지만 조금 더 일반적이고 덜 귀여운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '요리조리' but more general and less cute.

explain_en: It does not mean 'carelessly'; it means moving or looking this way and that, changing direction. It has a slightly cute, light tone. It suits the movements of children and animals especially well.

en: to snarl; to growl; to roar

examples.en: The puppy growls when it sees a stranger.
I was scared to walk past the growling dog.

examples.ko: 고양이 두 마리가 서로 으르렁거리고 있어요.
examples.en: Two cats are snarling at each other.
When the lion roared, the kids were startled.
Those brothers snarl at each other whenever they meet.
If a dog growls, don't go near it.

explain: 개, 고양이, 사자 같은 동물이 화가 나서 낮고 거칠게 소리를 낼 때 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 서로 사이가 나빠서 거칠게 말하거나 싸울 듯이 대한다는 비유가 돼요. 흔히 '서로 으르렁거리다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The two dogs growled at each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으르렁거리다'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 줄여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 으르렁거리다, shorter in speech.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 만나기만 하면 서로 으르렁거려요.
phrases.en: Those two snarl at each other whenever they meet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 사이가 나쁠 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when people are on bad terms.

phrases.en: I heard a growling sound in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물의 낮은 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an animal's low sound.

explain_en: It describes animals like dogs, cats and lions making a low, rough sound when angry. About people, it figuratively means being on bad terms and speaking harshly as if ready to fight. It is commonly used as '서로 으르렁거리다'.

en: to talk to oneself; to mumble to oneself

examples.en: Grandfather sometimes talks to himself.
When I study, talking to myself helps me focus.
He talked to himself while walking down the street.
I can hear that person talking to themselves.
My little brother is talking to himself in his room.
What are you muttering to yourself like that?

explain: 듣는 사람 없이 혼자 말할 때 써요. 작게 중얼거리는 소리는 '중얼거리다', 입 안에서 웅얼거리는 소리는 '웅얼거리다'라고 해서 모양이 달라요. 보통은 명사 '혼잣말'을 써서 '혼잣말을 하다'라고 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is talking to himself in the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '혼잣말하다'보다 이 모양이 말할 때 더 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: This form is heard more often in speech than '혼잣말하다'.

phrases.en: He spoke quietly, as if talking to himself.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-듯이'를 붙여서 혼자 말하는 것처럼 작게 말하는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-듯이' describes speaking softly as if to oneself.
phrases.en_equiv: to speak as if to oneself

phrases.en: I have a habit of talking to myself.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는 버릇'을 붙여서 자주 하는 습관을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-는 버릇' describes a habit someone often has.
phrases.en_equiv: a habit of talking to oneself

explain_en: It is used when someone talks with no listener. Quiet muttering is '중얼거리다' and mumbling inside the mouth is '웅얼거리다', so the picture differs. People more often use the noun '혼잣말' and say '혼잣말을 하다'.

examples.en: He whistled because he was in a good mood.
A whistling sound echoes in the alley.

examples.ko: 밤에 휘파람을 불면 안 된다고 해요.
examples.en: They say you shouldn't whistle at night.
My friend sent a signal by whistling.
Please teach me how to whistle.
The puppy ran over at the sound of the whistle.

explain: '휘파람을 불다'로 짝지어 써요. '노래를 부르다'의 '부르다'가 아니라 '불다'라서 헷갈리지 않게 주의하세요. 한국에는 '밤에 휘파람을 불면 뱀이 나온다'는 옛말이 있어요.

phrases.en: He walked away whistling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휘파람을 불면서 다른 행동을 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when doing another action while whistling.

phrases.en: Whistling is still hard for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휘파람을 부는 일 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the act of whistling itself.

phrases.en: I'll try whistling too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'를 붙여서 한번 해 본다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -아/어 보다 means to try it once.

explain_en: It pairs with the verb '불다' as in '휘파람을 불다'. It is '불다', not the '부르다' of '노래를 부르다', so watch out for mixing them up. Korea has an old saying, '밤에 휘파람을 불면 뱀이 나온다'.
